what_its_for: Cabotegravir and rilpivirine is a combination medicine used to treat HIV-1 infection in adults and teenagers (12 years and older weighing at least 35 kg) who are already stable on HIV treatment and whose virus is well controlled (undetectable). It does NOT cure HIV, but it helps keep the virus under control so your immune system can stay healthy and reduce your risk of getting sick.
how_to_take: This medicine comes as two separate injectable shots given by your doctor or nurse at a clinic or hospital — you do NOT inject it yourself at home. Both shots are given on the same day, one in each buttock (gluteal muscle). You will first take cabotegravir and rilpivirine pills by mouth for one month (called the 'lead-in' period) to make sure you tolerate the medicines before switching to the injections. After that, you will get the injections once a month or once every two months, depending on what your doctor decides is best for you. Never miss your scheduled injection appointments — staying on schedule is very important for keeping your HIV under control.
dosing: The standard injection dose is cabotegravir 600 mg plus rilpivirine 900 mg given as two separate shots on the same day. For the every-two-month schedule, the dose is cabotegravir 600 mg plus rilpivirine 900 mg given once every 2 months. Before starting injections, you may take one cabotegravir 30 mg tablet and one rilpivirine 25 mg tablet by mouth once daily with a meal for about 4 weeks. Your doctor will decide the exact schedule and dose that is right for you.
missed_dose: If you miss or need to reschedule an injection appointment, contact your doctor or clinic right away. Do NOT skip your injection without talking to your doctor first. If your injection is going to be very late, your doctor may prescribe temporary oral HIV medicines to take until you can get your next injection. Missing injections can allow the virus to become detectable again and may cause the virus to become resistant to this medicine, making it harder to treat in the future.
storage: The injections are stored and prepared by your healthcare provider at the clinic — you do not need to store them at home. If you are given oral cabotegravir or rilpivirine tablets, store them at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep tablets in their original container, away from moisture and heat, and out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush medicines down the toilet unless the label tells you to. Ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of any unused medicines.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT take certain medicines while using cabotegravir and rilpivirine, as they can make your HIV medicine stop working. Tell your doctor about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take. Avoid: antiseizure medicines like carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, phenobarbital, or phenytoin; rifampin, rifapentine, or rifabutin (used for tuberculosis); antacids or supplements containing aluminum, magnesium, or calcium within 2 hours before or 4 hours after taking the oral tablets; the herbal supplement St. John's Wort; metformin in high doses without your doctor's guidance; and dexamethasone (more than a single dose). Avoid sharing needles, syringes, or personal items like razors or toothbrushes that may have contact with blood, as HIV can still be spread to others even on this treatment.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, trouble breathing, or dizziness; severe pain, swelling, redness, or drainage at the injection site that does not go away; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, nausea, or stomach pain; mood changes, depression, thoughts of self-harm, or suicidal thoughts; symptoms of a serious skin reaction such as blistering, peeling, or sores in your mouth; signs of infection such as fever, chills, or feeling very unwell; or if you think you may be pregnant, are planning to get pregnant, or are breastfeeding.
when_it_works: Cabotegravir and rilpivirine starts working right away after your first injection, but you may not feel any different because HIV often causes no symptoms. The goal of treatment is to keep the amount of virus in your blood very low (undetectable). Most people who take this medicine consistently as scheduled maintain an undetectable viral load. It is very important to keep ALL of your injection appointments, even if you feel well, because HIV can come back quickly if doses are missed.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. This medicine is not recommended during pregnancy because it may stay in your body for a long time, and its safety during pregnancy is not fully established. Use effective birth control while taking this medicine. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed if you have HIV, as the virus can be passed to your baby through breast milk. Teenagers: This medicine can be used in teenagers 12 years and older who weigh at least 35 kg (about 77 lbs). Kidney or liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as your doctor may need to adjust your treatment plan or monitor you more closely. Older adults: There is limited information on use in older adults, but no specific dose adjustment is currently recommended.
